title: Intro to Machine Learning

points: ML lets computers learn patterns from data without explicit programming
Three main types: supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning
Supervised learning learns from labeled training data
Performance is measured on held-out test data
Classification predicts a category; regression predicts a number
Training data pairs each input with a correct label
Overfitting means memorizing training data instead of learning patterns
Common algorithms: linear regression, decision trees, k-nearest neighbors
Unsupervised learning finds hidden structure in unlabeled data
Clustering groups similar examples, e.g. k-means
Reinforcement learning learns from rewards and penalties
An agent takes actions in an environment to maximize cumulative reward

options: Learning patterns from data without explicit programming
quiz.why: ML is defined by learning patterns from data instead of following hand-written rules.

quiz.q: Which type of machine learning uses labeled training data?
quiz.why: Supervised learning pairs each input with a correct label during training.

options: The model memorizes training data and does poorly on new data
The test set is too large
quiz.why: Overfitting means the model learned noise and specifics of the training set instead of general patterns.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a test set?
options: To measure performance on unseen data
quiz.why: A test set is held out from training to estimate how the model performs on new examples.
k-means groups unlabeled data into clusters without any labels.
An agent improves by maximizing cumulative reward through trial and error.

quiz.q: What is the difference between classification and regression?
options: Classification predicts categories; regression predicts numbers
Classification is unsupervised; regression is supervised
Regression predicts categories; classification predicts numbers
quiz.why: Classification outputs a class label, while regression outputs a continuous value.

quiz.q: What is the goal of clustering?
quiz.why: Clustering finds natural groups in unlabeled data by similarity.
